result.markdown: --- title: >- [scrape.find_links()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Discover links by crawling one or more starting pages. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/raghilda/blob/docs-embedding-providers/src/raghilda/scrape.py#L46-L201){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python scrape.find_links( x, depth=0, children_only=False, progress=True, *, url_filter=None, validate=False, **request_kwargs ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `find_links()` is the simple way to gather a set of URLs to index: give it a starting page (or several) and it follows links up to `depth` levels before returning the URLs it finds. It reads both HTML pages (following `` links) and XML sitemaps (collecting their `` entries). This function is eager: it completes the crawl before returning the list of discovered URLs. For a lazy version of this same URL discovery step, see [`WebCrawler.origins()`](crawl.WebCrawler.qmd#raghilda.crawl.WebCrawler.origins). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [x]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | Path | Sequence[str | Path]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Starting URL(s) or path(s): a single string or `Path`, or a sequence of them. [depth]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum traversal depth from each starting page. `0` inspects the starting pages only, `1` also follows their direct links, and so on. [children_only]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : When `True`, only links at or below the starting URL are kept and followed (for example links under `https://site/docs/` when you start there). This is the easiest way to stay within one section of a site. [progress]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to display a `tqdm` progress bar while crawling. [url_filter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Callable[[set[str]], list[str]] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional callback that receives the set of links found on a page and returns the (possibly smaller) list of URLs to keep and follow. Use it to apply custom include/exclude rules. [validate]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : When `True`, check that each URL is reachable (with an HTTP `HEAD` request) before including it in the results. [request_kwargs]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [{}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Extra keyword arguments forwarded to `requests.Session.get` (and to `head` during validation) when fetching pages. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A deduplicated list of absolute URLs discovered during the crawl. The crawl completes before this list is returned. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#dc6332f9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from raghilda.scrape import find_links # Discover pages under a documentation section, one level deep links = find_links( "https://quarto.org/docs/guide/", depth=1, children_only=True, ) print(f"Found {len(links)} pages") ``` :::
